clips.title: OpenTelemetry Concepts for AI: Span, Trace, Session
clips.why: How an AI application's many calls are tied together by a shared ID, so one conversation can be read as one thing.
look: Going from one model call to a multi-turn conversation: many records that belong together.
A session ID put on every record is what lets a tool group them later.
Compare it with our five tags: the run and the step are the IDs that group a run's numbers.
clips.after: We do the same with metrics instead of traces: every number of a step carries agent, jira, run, step and harness.version, so Grafana can group cost by any of them.

clips.title: I Put Langfuse on My AI Agent - It Found My Money Leak
clips.why: A real agent's cost split into its steps, and the one step that was quietly spending most of the money.
look: The total cost alone says nothing about where to look; the split does.
How the expensive part shows up once each call is grouped by what it was doing.
Ask yourself which of Nova's nine steps you would check first if the build step were not the expensive one.
clips.after: Our Friday question, "where did RH-1234's $4.10 go?", is answered the same way, with the step tag instead of a tracing tool.

clips.title: Error Analysis: The Highest ROI Technique In AI Engineering
clips.why: Why the most useful thing to do with an AI system's failures is to look at real ones and write down what went wrong.
look: Reading real runs (he calls them traces) instead of guessing from a score.
Writing a short note on each failure, in your own words, before inventing categories.
clips.after: Our weekly run review is this habit: five runs a week, each failure written down as where it failed, where it should have been caught, and why.

clips.title: Error Analysis: The Highest ROI Technique In AI Engineering
clips.why: From notes to numbers: grouping failures into a few categories and counting them, so you know which problem to fix first.
look: How free-text notes become a small set of categories.
Counting the categories tells you where the next week of work should go.
clips.after: Our run labels use fixed lists for steps and causes so the nightly job can count them, and a label seen twice in a month becomes a ticket.

practice.q: Finish the line in the harness so the build session keeps the gateway address and the run token and also gets its five tags.
practice.hint: Spread the harness's own environment first.
practice.why: options.env replaces the session's environment. Without the spread, the session starts with nothing but the tags and cannot reach the gateway.

practice.q: Which variable does every OpenTelemetry SDK, Claude Code included, read at start to label everything it sends?

options.why: A comma-separated list of name=value pairs, attached to every metric and event the process sends.
Those are HTTP headers on the requests to the collector, such as the ingest token. They are not labels on the data.
Those headers go on model calls to the gateway. They label the gateway's own counters, not Claude Code's telemetry.

practice.q: Put these in order for the build step of RH-1234.
items: The workflow enters the build step and sets the Step search attribute to build
The harness builds the env: process.env plus stepEnv(run, "build")
It starts a new query() session with that env
Claude Code reads OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES at start and labels every number with step=build
In Grafana, the build step's cost appears next to the other steps and they add up to the gateway total
practice.why: The tags are decided before the session starts, because a process reads its environment only once.

practice.q: A run failed in review: Byte found that the change broke a public API that the plan never listed. Which label fits?

options.text: failed_at byte, should_have_caught plan, cause missing_context
options.why: It broke at Byte's review, the plan should have listed the API, and the plan lacked that context.

options.text: failed_at plan, should_have_caught byte, cause model
options.why: Swapped: nothing failed in the plan step. Byte caught it, too late; the plan is where it should have been stopped.

options.text: failed_at byte, should_have_caught byte, cause unknown
options.why: Byte did catch it. The useful column is the earlier step that let it through.

practice.q: A plan was approved 20 seconds after Nova asked. What does the nightly job do with that?

options.why: There is no score per person anywhere in the platform.

options.text: Lists the run's link for the weekly review, so someone looks at that run
options.why: Fast approvals flag a run, never rank a person. Twenty seconds is too short to read a plan, so the run deserves a look.

options.text: Cancels the approval and asks again
options.why: The job only reads records the next night. It never changes a run.
